From:   http://wiki.freepascal.org/Clarification_on_the_GPL
# GFDL ===> Public Domain, which permits to release a re-distribution.
# GNU FDL: Aka General Public Licence v.3.0 -> 2007 http://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html ===> Allows modification which can only be sold under free software/ free docs which contains the original, modified and changed files.
# GPL/Artistic-License: Allows modification which can be sold, if both are included with the sold/distributed product. Or modify a file, and create a new file that replaces the file you modified with a new edited file. Giving a download that is mod. into a new file is forbidden, but the modified file is for free. Artistic_2.0/GPL 2.0 licence: Allows commercialization or closed source licensing if both are combined.
#  LGP (Lesser GNU Public Licence -> 1999 -> www.gnu.org/copyleft/lesser.html ===> A variant license that uses GPL compatible licences(like GPL, Free Document Foundation license) under an added Lesser GPL restriction of requiring recipricate linking for non-complimental software. But the only benefit from this, is that the added restriction does not cause free software(as defined by RMS) to lose any right, instead making linking non-complimentary free software in compliance with LGP illegal/not-possible, without violating GPL's first 10/12 points.
# MIT/Public-Domain (1990->MIT-licence: Allows modification under any type of license and distribution under any other type of license, with only condition of crediting the original work. Forbidding redistribution as binary, while still possible. But allows redistribution as a source-copy (by source) in binary form.
# X11= (Mix 11=BSD-copyright/MIT-licence) X11 Copyright licence 2006->http://www.x11.org/copyright-license.html ===> Any of the three main permits(MIT, Free BSD and GPL) are allow.
# AGPL 2006/3->http://www.fsf.org/wiki/License:AGPL_v3.0 ===> Same as GPL 2+, that also allow modification and redistribution of source files, but does not offer any recipricator linking unless modified in ways that make it not GPL compatible. Same problems with commercial, proprietary software under the new license. That's why it isn't mentioned on here, as AGPL makes little progress over GPL 2/3.
